Scheduling notes
What the draft keeps about each person, dated, until it ends.
Operational Score
Rate each person 1 to 5 — 1 very weak, 3 average, 5 excellent. The scheduler uses this to balance who works together, never to bench anybody. Nothing changes in your schedules until somebody is rated.
Name
Role (optional)
{# Who changed a rating, a target or the weighting, and when (GET /api/labor/capability-changes; memory round 9/29/26, M7). #}
Shift strength targets
What a full crew of the role scores together on your busiest shift for it. Each shift is judged per person against that share: a target of 8 for a crew of two bartenders asks for about 4 a person, so a lunch with one bartender is held to about 4, not 8 — and adding a body never buys strength. Unrated people aren’t counted either way. Leave a role blank for no target.
Shift leader requirements
Stricter than a target: this names one person who has to be on that shift.

Each shift is scored 0–100 on coverage, operational strength, leadership, experience, training balance, demand match and labor efficiency. A profile sets the bar for the shifts it names.

Gaps in your public record

Your reviews, replies and Google listing — the gaps you still have come first.
What happens when you improve this?
We check one AI search system — Perplexity — by asking it the kinds of questions a guest would, and seeing whether you come up. What it answers from is Perplexity's business, not something we can see. What we can tell you is that these items are the public record of your restaurant: your reviews, your replies, and the fields on your Google listing. Most independent restaurants have gaps here. Closing them is the part that's in your hands.

How you serveThe split every comparison respects: a counter spot is never compared with a full-service dining room.
ConceptWhat the menu is built on — it decides which food-cost comparisons are fair.
Bar-ledAlcohol is about 40% or more of sales. Drinks carry little labor, so it changes what a fair labor % is.

Targets & pay rates

What labor and food cost are judged against, and what each hour costs. Every labor figure and every drafted week’s budget uses these.

Labor targetLabor as a % of sales. The schedule is drafted to it.
Food cost targetFood cost as a % of food sales.
Waste targetWaste as a % of purchases. Blank uses Cavnar AI’s starting 4.5%.
Monthly revenue targetYour weekly target × 4.33 (52 weeks over 12 months). Blank or 0 means no target.
Weekly revenue targetIn dollars. Type either one and the other fills in — it’s one target.
Blended hourly rateWhat an hour costs when nobody in its role has a rate. Everyone else is costed at their own pay.
Payroll week startsOvertime is counted over this week.
Hourly pay
Salaried staffpaid a salary, not by the hour · shown beside hourly labor, never in it
Only the account owner can change targets and pay rates.

Nightly report and weekly grid

Build the daily report every nightAfter close, from the POS. Owner logins get the owner report; manager logins get the manager report.

Period 1, Week 1 startsLeave it blank for weeks only, with no period numbers.
PeriodsThirteen periods of four weeks, quarters of 4-4-5, 4-5-4 or 5-4-4 weeks, or your accounting system’s own lengths.

Automation, AI & memory

What the AI may do on its own, how it sounds, and what it remembers.

Work Cavnar AI does for you

Drafting the schedule, sending it, ordering from suppliers you trust — each one off until you turn it on, and each one undoable.

Draft next week’s schedule for meEvery Thursday, if you haven’t built one. A draft only — nothing goes to staff until you publish. On by default with a paid Labor plan; switch it off any time.
{# The owner's day for the draft and for trusted orders (9/27/26): Thursday and Monday were fixed. Mirrored by the day in the Studio's AI tab and on What to order this week. #}
Draft dayIt drafts the week that starts the next Monday, from 6am that day — so Monday to Saturday. Publish it for me goes the day after.
Plan my week for meMonday mornings Cavnar AI reads the week — brief, issues, goals, results, what connects — and files up to three owned actions under Still open. Nobody is texted.
Give me a moment before anything goes outA supplier order or a published schedule waits this long with an Undo in the Cavnar AI strip before it leaves the building.
Send orders to suppliers you’ve used beforeMonday mornings, an order to a supplier with 3+ past orders, for about what you usually spend, goes out an hour later — you’re told, and can undo from Home. New suppliers always wait for you.
Order dayTrusted orders are queued at 8am that day, with an hour to undo.
Publish it for me on FridayOnce your last 3 published schedules went out unedited, the Thursday draft goes to staff at 11am Friday — you’re told at 9, and can undo from Home until then.

Auto-approve 5-star replies

Drafted replies to 5-star reviews are approved automatically — and posted, when Google Business is connected. Capped per day, with a pause switch.

Turn on auto-approveOnly 5-star reviews. Everything else still waits for you.
Include 4-star reviewsSame ceiling, same rule: anything the analyser flags still waits for you. Never 3 stars or below.
Extend it as you earn itOnce you’ve approved 10 replies on a star band in 30 days and edited at most 1 in 10, that band goes out on its own too — 3★ at most, never lower.
Most replies per dayA ceiling, so a busy weekend can’t post fifty replies unread.
Pause it for nowKeeps the rule and the cap; nothing posts until you unpause.
Daily ceiling5 / 50

Getting started
Will personally sets up every restaurant — connecting your Google Business Profile, POS system, and configuring the modules you're paying for. You won't need to do any technical setup yourself; if something looks disconnected or missing, contact Will.
Reviews drafts AI responses to your Google reviews and flags urgent ones. Intel tracks what's being said about you and nearby competitors. Marketing automates guest outreach. Labor pulls hours and schedules from your POS. Food Cost tracks ingredient spend and waste. Not every restaurant has every module — see Billing for what's active on yours.
Reviews
Only if you turn on the auto-approve rule under Automation & AI, and then only for 5-star reviews, capped per day. Everything else needs your approval before it goes out — edit the draft, approve it as-is, or regenerate it from the review's detail screen.
Two kinds: a 1- or 2-star review from the last 30 days that hasn’t been answered yet, and any review about illness, injury, a legal threat or staff misconduct. Urgent reviews sit at the top of your list until they’re answered. The safety and legal ones can also send you an alert, depending on your alert settings.
Security
2FA adds a one-time code (by email or text) on top of your password at sign-in. Once it's on, you'll also get a set of one-time backup codes — save them somewhere safe in case you ever lose access to your email or phone.
Yes — the account owner can add teammates under People (or in the iOS app under Account → Manage team). Each teammate gets their own real login, and the owner can remove access at any time. Employees are different: they use the staff portal with a PIN and never see this dashboard.
Billing & account
Payment method and invoices are under Billing. To add or remove a module, or change anything on your contract, contact Will directly.
Yes — use Export my data under Data & privacy (or in the iOS app under Account → Export my data). It emails you CSVs of your reviews, labor and food cost history, plus a JSON of your settings.
Getting started with Cavnar AI includes signing a service agreement, so cancellation isn't self-serve — use Request cancellation under Data & privacy. 30 days' written notice is required; your account stays active through the end of your current billing period plus 30 days.
Notifications
Manage alerts (under Notifications) controls what triggers an alert — 1-star reviews, a rating spike, health mentions, and so on — and whether it reaches you by text, email, or push, plus optional quiet hours.
Alerts are near-real-time — something specific just happened. The weekly digest is a full summary sent on the day you choose.
